faqs.question: Is Choti Diwali on 28 or 29 October 2027?
faqs.answer: Thursday 28 October 2027. Friday 29 October is Lakshmi Puja, the main Diwali night; the Chaturdashi tithi that defines Choti Diwali runs from 10:49 PM on 27 October to 8:47 PM on 28 October (New Delhi, Drik Panchang).

faqs.question: What time should I take the abhyanga snan if I live in Chennai?
faqs.answer: Between 04:40 and 06:01 AM on Thursday 28 October 2027, per Drik Panchang set to Chennai. In New Delhi the window is 05:06 to 06:30 AM, so do not copy a North Indian time for a South Indian city.

faqs.question: Is Roop Chaudas the same day as Choti Diwali this year?
faqs.answer: Yes. Roop Chaudas, Roop Chaturdashi, Narak Chaturdashi and Choti Diwali are names for the same Chaturdashi day, and in 2027 that is Thursday 28 October.

faqs.question: Will offices in Chennai close on 28 or 29 October 2027?
faqs.answer: Unknown as of October 2026. Third-party holiday calendars print 29 October as an estimate, while the panchang puts Tamil Deepavali on 28 October; wait for the Tamil Nadu government's official 2027 holiday order.

faqs.question: When is Kali Chaudas in 2027?
faqs.answer: Wednesday 27 October 2027, a day before Narak Chaturdashi. Drik Panchang gives the Kali Chaudas muhurat as 11:39 PM to 12:31 AM, because it follows Chaturdashi at midnight rather than before dawn.

faqs.question: Was Choti Diwali 2026 on the same day as Diwali?
faqs.answer: Yes, effectively. Chaturdashi ran from 10:47 AM on 7 November to 11:27 AM on 8 November 2026, so the oil bath and Lakshmi Puja both fell on Sunday 8 November. In 2027 they separate into Thursday and Friday.

faqs.question: Who killed Narakasura, Krishna or Satyabhama?
faqs.answer: In the Vishnu Purana (Book V, Section XXIX) Krishna cuts Naraka in two with his discus while Satyabhama rides with him on Garuda. Versions in which Satyabhama strikes the blow come from later regional retellings.

faqs.question: Can I still do the oil bath after sunrise?
faqs.answer: By the panchang rule, no: the abhyang snan window runs from moonrise to sunrise while Chaturdashi lasts, which on 28 October 2027 ends at 06:30 AM in Delhi. Many families still bathe later; it simply falls outside the prescribed muhurat.

faqs.question: How do I keep diyas safe on Choti Diwali night?
faqs.answer: Keep them on a raised, non-combustible surface away from doorways, curtains and loose synthetic clothing. A Safdarjung Hospital review found 32.5% of Diwali-period burns came from diyas, mostly from a lit diya left on the floor.

faqs.question: Should I send Diwali wishes on Choti Diwali or wait for Friday?
faqs.answer: Either works, but Thursday evening gives them a day to open it. In SubhSandesh's Raksha Bandhan 2026 data (n = 89, the nearest festival analogue) 27.0% of pages were built the day before and 49.4% on the day.

faqs.question: Will the SubhSandesh Diwali page open properly if they get it on 28 October?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Happy Diwali page works on any date, opens in any phone or laptop browser without an app or account, and the link keeps working so they can open it again on Diwali night.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Choti Diwali 2027: The Thursday Before Lakshmi Puja, Hour by Hour

Choti Diwali 2027 falls on **Thursday, 28 October 2027**. It is Narak Chaturdashi, also called Roop Chaudas, and it sits between Dhanteras on Wednesday 27 October and Lakshmi Puja on Friday 29 October. The Chaturdashi tithi runs from 10:49 PM on 27 October to 8:47 PM on 28 October, and the pre-dawn oil bath window in New Delhi is 05:06 to 06:30 AM, per [Drik Panchang's 2027 abhyang snan timings](https://www.drikpanchang.com/festivals/abhyangsnan/festivals-abhyangsnan-timings.html?year=2027).

If you plan to send a greeting, this is the evening most people actually do it. In SubhSandesh's Raksha Bandhan 2026 data, used here as the nearest festival analogue (n = 89), 27.0% of pages were built the day before the festival and 49.4% on the day itself, and 48.3% of all shared pages are opened on a phone. Below: the timings, why Tamil Nadu treats this morning as Deepavali, the Narakasura story as the Vishnu Purana tells it, and what moves to a different day in 2027.

## What is Choti Diwali, and why does it have three names?

Choti Diwali is the second day of the five-day Diwali festival, observed on the Chaturdashi (14th lunar day) of the dark fortnight that ends in the Diwali new moon. "Choti" simply means small: it is the eve of the main night, with fewer lamps and a lighter puja.

The other two names describe what the day is for. Narak Chaturdashi remembers Krishna's victory over the asura Naraka, and Roop Chaudas (or Roop Chaturdashi) points to the beauty bath of oil and ubtan that families take before sunrise. Drik Panchang lists all three as names of the same day, and in 2027 all three land on 28 October.

## Choti Diwali 2027 timings for Delhi and Chennai

The bath is fixed by two conditions: the Chaturdashi tithi must be running, and the moon must have risen while the sky is still dark. In 2027 both hold on the morning of Thursday 28 October. Times shift by city because sunrise and moonrise do.

- **New Delhi:** abhyang snan 05:06 to 06:30 AM, 1 hour 24 minutes.
- **Chennai:** 04:40 to 06:01 AM, 1 hour 21 minutes (the same Drik Panchang page, set to Chennai).
- **Chaturdashi tithi:** 10:49 PM on 27 October to 8:47 PM on 28 October 2027.
- **Amavasya** begins as Chaturdashi ends, on the night of 28 October, which is why Friday 29 October carries Lakshmi Puja.

Check your own city before setting an alarm. Delhi and Chennai start 26 minutes apart, enough to miss the window.

## Why Tamil Nadu's Deepavali morning is this day

In Tamil Nadu, Deepavali itself is observed when Chaturdashi prevails during Brahma muhurta, just before sunrise, according to [Drik Panchang's note on Tamil festival rules](https://www.drikpanchang.com/festivals/tamil-festivals.html?year=2027). North India keys the main festival to Amavasya in the evening, for Lakshmi Puja at dusk. One festival, two clocks: Tamil Nadu counts the dawn, Delhi counts the dusk.

That is why [Drik Panchang's 2027 Diwali calendar](https://www.drikpanchang.com/diwali/diwali-puja-calendar.html?year=2027) marks **Tamil Deepavali on Thursday 28 October**, the same day as Narak Chaturdashi. In a Chennai home the oil bath, new clothes, sweets and the first crackers all happen that morning. In a Lucknow home the same Thursday is a quieter eve.

In 2026 the two clocks happened to agree. Chaturdashi ran from 10:47 AM on 7 November to 11:27 AM on 8 November 2026, so the bath and Lakshmi Puja both fell on Sunday 8 November. In 2027 they split across Thursday and Friday.

One inconvenient detail, as of October 2026: third-party holiday calendars currently print 29 October as Deepavali for Tamil Nadu, and at least one labels its 2027 dates as an estimate. The state's official holiday notification for 2027 was not yet out when this was written. If you need leave or a school date, wait for the government order rather than trusting either calendar.

Morning crackers bring their own risk in the south. A [Bengaluru eye hospital's Deepavali case series (2010)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC2854452) recorded 51 patients with firecracker eye injuries; 29 of them were onlookers, not the people lighting, and none had worn eye protection.

## The Narakasura story, as the Vishnu Purana actually tells it

The oldest widely available telling is in the Vishnu Purana, Book V, Section XXIX, readable in the public-domain [Dutt translation based on H. H. Wilson on Project Gutenberg](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/66208). Indra comes to Dwarka to report that Naraka, son of Bhumi (the Earth) and ruler of Pragjyotisha, has seized Aditi's earrings and Varuna's umbrella and locked away captive maidens.

Krishna flies to Pragjyotisha on Garuda with Satyabhama seated beside him, cuts through the razor-edged nooses of the demon Mura, kills Mura, and then cuts Naraka in two with his discus. The Earth returns Aditi's earrings and asks forgiveness for her son, saying he was killed for his own purification. Krishna then frees 16,100 women held in Naraka's palace.

Two details many retellings change. In this text Krishna strikes the blow, not Satyabhama, and Naraka makes no dying request that his death be marked with lamps. Both belong to later regional tellings, not this translation, so if a grandparent tells it differently, neither of you is wrong: you are quoting different centuries.

## Choti Diwali 2027, hour by hour

Rituals vary by family, so treat this as the common spine, not a rulebook. All times are for 28 October 2027.

### 1. Before sunrise: abhyanga snan

The oil bath is the day's defining act: warm oil worked into the scalp and skin, then washed off, often with ubtan of gram flour and turmeric. In Delhi the window closes at 06:30 AM; in Chennai at 06:01 AM. In Tamil homes this is the Deepavali bath itself, followed by new clothes.

### 2. Morning: Roop Chaudas or Tamil Deepavali

In parts of western India the day leans towards Roop Chaudas, a grooming-and-beauty morning. Tamil households move straight into Deepavali visits, sweets and crackers, all on Thursday this year.

### 3. Evening: the first full row of diyas

Choti Diwali evening brings the first full row of diyas in many homes, a rehearsal for Friday, so keep them off the floor where people walk. A [five-year review of Diwali burns at Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi (2024)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11684968) found that 32.5% of Diwali-period burns came from diyas, that a burning diya left on the floor was the main cause, and that 70.4% of those injured were women. The authors advise keeping diyas on a non-combustible surface and avoiding loose synthetic clothing near them.

### 4. Night: Amavasya arrives

Chaturdashi ends at 8:47 PM on 28 October and Amavasya begins. Drik Panchang lists Bengal's Kali Puja on the night of 28 October, so Kolkata's main night is Thursday, not Friday.

## What moves to a different day in 2027

Because Chaturdashi starts late on Wednesday night, two observances people associate with Choti Diwali fall a day earlier. Drik Panchang lists **Kali Chaudas** (observed mostly in Gujarat) and **Hanuman Puja** on Wednesday 27 October 2027, with the Kali Chaudas muhurat from 11:39 PM to 12:31 AM. **Yama Deepam** also falls on 27 October, alongside Dhanteras, because Kali Chaudas follows midnight Chaturdashi while Narak Chaturdashi follows the pre-dawn moon.

## Sending a Choti Diwali greeting: the night before is when people build

There is no Diwali creation data on SubhSandesh yet, because the Diwali page is new, so the nearest honest evidence is Raksha Bandhan 2026 (n = 89, a one-day festival, small sample). Mapped onto the 2027 calendar, the pattern looks like this.

| Diwali 2027 day | Date | Offset from Lakshmi Puja | Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages built at that offset (n = 89) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dhanteras | Wed 27 Oct | 2 days before | 5.6% (two to three days ahead) |
| Choti Diwali | Thu 28 Oct | 1 day before | 27.0% |
| Lakshmi Puja | Fri 29 Oct | The day itself | 49.4% |
| Govardhan Puja, Bhai Dooj | Sat 30 to Sun 31 Oct | After | 11.2% |

Of the 79 rakhi pages finished in time, 86.1% were built within 24 hours of the festival. If Diwali follows that shape, Thursday evening, after the Choti Diwali diyas, is the realistic build window.

That is where the [interactive Happy Diwali card on SubhSandesh](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) fits. It is a one-person page: they light a diya at their door with your tag on it, a row of wish diyas, a rangoli that glows with your initials and sky lanterns holding up to six photos, then open your letter from a shagun liffafa. It takes about five minutes, has love, family and friend modes, and opens in any phone browser without an app, and a shared page averages 11.1 views, so a link sent Thursday night can be reopened on Friday.

These three Choti Diwali lines were written for this post; copy any of them into the letter or a message. Each works for family or a friend.

- "Tomorrow is the big night. Tonight is for the people who made the house bright enough for it."
- "May the oil bath wash off the year's tiredness and leave only the good parts."
- "छोटी दिवाली की रौशनी, बड़ी दिवाली से पहले तुम तक। (Chhoti Diwali ki raushni, badi Diwali se pehle tum tak.) Choti Diwali's light, reaching you before the big one."

## When a link is the wrong Choti Diwali gesture

A page does not replace being there for the 5 AM bath at your grandmother's, and it is no help with the puja itself; it is not a muhurat or ritual tool. It suits one person, not a family WhatsApp group of forty. And since only 48.3% of opens are on a phone, an elder who never opens links is better served by a call at 6 AM.

If the person you are missing this Thursday is a partner in another city, the [I miss you page](https://subhsandesh.in/missyou-gf) says that more directly than a festival card. If they are on a train home for the Friday holiday, the [Train Ticket love letter](https://subhsandesh.in/train-ticket), with its PNR check and clearing waitlist, fits the journey better.
